name: CA-38
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting D+8 district lean combined with a favorable national environment
Hilda Solis has raised $1.4 million while Pedro Casas shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 98 percent
Open seat with no public polls, leaving wider-than-usual uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's D+8 lean plus a favorable environment points to a high-teens Democratic margin, and Solis's lopsided fundraising edge over a Republican with no visible war chest reinforces that picture. Markets price her near-certain, and no evidence cuts the other way.
model.watch: Any late Republican outside spending or an unexpected Solis stumble could narrow the margin, though the structural lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 38th District, redrawn to lean Democratic by about eight points, is open this cycle, and Democrat Hilda Solis enters as the clear favorite. She has raised roughly $1.4 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Republican Pedro Casas shows no reported fundraising. Outside groups have spent modestly to support Solis and nothing to oppose her, and prediction markets price her chances near 98 percent.

No public polls cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, the national environment, and the lopsided money race. Those fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic margin in the high teens. With no expert ratings available and limited visibility into voter sentiment, uncertainty is somewhat wider than usual, but every visible indicator favors Solis.
